decision_reasoning: The hypothetical issuer directly controls cislunar and lunar-surface productive assets, has enforceable command and economic rights, and exceeds the project materiality and concentration presumptions on multiple independently stated metrics. This example remains unverified project-proposal output.

qualifying_nexus.summary: The intended issuer controls a cislunar relay, a lunar prospecting unit, and a cislunar logistics vehicle used directly in revenue-producing operations.

metrics.numerator_description: Enforceable contracted backlog requiring cislunar or lunar-surface performance.
metrics.methodology: Contracts are attributed only when performance requires qualifying beyond-Earth operations; terrestrial support-only contracts are excluded from the numerator.
metrics.uncertainty: Customer termination rights may reduce realized revenue but do not change signed backlog classification at the assessment date.

metrics.numerator_description: Replacement-cost estimate for qualifying cislunar and lunar-surface productive assets and directly attributable control systems.
metrics.denominator_description: Replacement-cost estimate for all consolidated productive assets.
metrics.methodology: Shared terrestrial support systems are allocated based on documented operational use rather than grossed entirely into the numerator.
metrics.uncertainty: Replacement-cost estimates depend on launch pricing and asset-specific remaining useful life.

metrics.numerator_description: Board-approved committed capital expenditure for qualifying fleet expansion, lunar equipment, and cislunar relay capacity.
metrics.denominator_description: Total board-approved committed capital expenditure over the next 24 months.
metrics.methodology: Only funded or contractually committed project capital is counted.
metrics.uncertainty: Schedule changes may move spending between periods.

material_dependence.summary: Multiple qualifying metrics exceed both the 25% materiality presumption and the 50% concentration presumption.

rights_control.summary: The intended issuer is represented as holding economic title or enforceable capacity rights to the material assets, command authority within documented control boundaries, and the customer revenue/data rights generated by those operations.

evidence_sufficiency.summary: The hypothetical assessment references recent asset, contract, budget, and control evidence sufficient for a project-level classification, but no factual claims have been independently verified by open-ipo.

anti_gaming_checks.summary: Backlog is counted based on required beyond-Earth performance, not merely because the customer participates in the space sector.
Shared terrestrial support infrastructure is allocated to the numerator only to the extent economically attributable to qualifying operations.
Backlog, asset, and capex percentages are presented as separate indicators and are not summed into a combined eligibility score.
The classification is supported by economic activity, rights, and operational dependence rather than the mere fact that autonomous agents control parts of the fleet.

uncertainties: Productive-asset replacement cost is sensitive to future launch pricing and remaining useful-life assumptions.
Backlog may not equal realized revenue because customer termination and mission-performance conditions remain applicable.

verification.summary: This is a fictional worked example. The structure demonstrates the proposed assessment contract; open-ipo has not independently verified any issuer fact.

disclaimer: Illustrative project-proposal assessment only. It is not an adopted Orbital Exchange eligibility determination, securities approval, legal classification, regulatory approval, or investment recommendation.
